solutions.latex: $y = \dfrac{-3x-5}{4}$, so the gradient is $-\dfrac{3}{4}$. Answer A.

Original average $= \dfrac{90+78+81+83}{4} = \dfrac{332}{4} = 83\%$. New mean $= 84\%$.

$\dfrac{x+332}{5} = 84$, so $x = 5\times 84 - 332 = 88\%$. Answer C.

$\tan\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}$, hypotenuse $= \sqrt{3^2+2^2} = \sqrt{13}$. $\tan$ positive, so $\theta$ is in quadrant 1 or 3; since $0<\theta<\pi$, quadrant 1. $\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{13}}$ (positive in Q1). Answer B.
$x$ must be $\ge 4$ and $y$ must be $\ge 0$. Domain $[4,\infty)$, Range $[0,\infty)$. Answer B.

$P(A|B) = \dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$, so $P(B) = \dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(A|B)} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.25} = 0.8$.

Alternatively, with a tree diagram: $0.25x = 0.2$, so $x = 0.8$. Answer D.
The velocity curve has 3 turning points, so the acceleration curve must have exactly 3 $x$-intercepts. This eliminates B, C, D. Answer A.
$\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln(\cos x) = \dfrac{\frac{d}{dx}\cos x}{\cos x} = \dfrac{-\sin x}{\cos x} = -\tan x$

A PDF has total area $1$, so the rectangle gives $0.2k = 1$, so $k = 5$.

Alternatively, $\displaystyle\int_0^k 0.2\,dx = 1$, $[0.2x]_0^k = 1$, $0.2k = 1$, $k=5$.

$\displaystyle\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx = \int_0^3 f(x)\,dx + \int_3^4 f(x)\,dx$

$15 = \displaystyle\int_0^3 f(x)\,dx - 5$, so $\displaystyle\int_0^3 f(x)\,dx = 20$.

$\displaystyle\int_{-1}^3 f(x)\,dx = \int_{-1}^0 f(x)\,dx + \int_0^3 f(x)\,dx = -4 + 20 = 16$

Expected profit per game $=$ cost per game $- \$1\times E(X) = \$3.50 - \$2.85 = \$0.65$.

Expected profit for 200 games $= 200\times\$0.65 = \$130$
$54 = \mu - 2\sigma$ and $98 = \mu + 2\sigma$, so by the empirical rule $P(54\le X\le 98) = 95\%$.

LHS $= (\sin x+\cos x)(\sec x - \operatorname{cosec} x)$

$= \sin x\sec x + \cos x\sec x - \sin x\operatorname{cosec} x - \cos x\operatorname{cosec} x$

$= \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \dfrac{\cos x}{\cos x} - \dfrac{\sin x}{\sin x} - \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}$

$= \tan x - \cot x = $ RHS

$\displaystyle\int x(x^2+5)^9\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int 2x(x^2+5)^9\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int f'(x)[f(x)]^n\,dx$ where $f(x) = x^2+5$, $n=9$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{n+1}[f(x)]^{n+1} + C = \dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{10}(x^2+5)^{10} + C = \dfrac{(x^2+5)^{10}}{20} + C$

Trapezoidal rule with $n = 4$ subintervals (not the number of function values), width $5$:

$\displaystyle\int_{20}^{40}f(x)\,dx \approx \dfrac{1}{2}\times 5\times\{10+20+2\times(12+25+28)\} = 400$

$\displaystyle\int_0^2 e^{2x}(3+6x)\,dx = 3\int_0^2 e^{2x}(1+2x)\,dx = 3\left[xe^{2x}\right]_0^2$ (from part (a), reverse chain rule)

$= 3\times(2e^{2\times 2} - 0) = 6e^4$

Use calculator for least squares regression line: $A = 90.920$, $B = -3.455$ where $y = A+Bx$.

$m = -3.455n + 90.920$ where $n$ = number of absences, $m$ = mark.

$f(x) = x^3+3x^2-9x$, $f'(x) = 3x^2+6x-9 = 3(x^2+2x-3) = 3(x+3)(x-1)$.

$f'(x) = 0$: $x=-3$ or $x=1$.

$f(-3) = (-3)^3 + 3(-3)^2 - 9(-3) = 27$; $f(1) = 1+3-9 = -5$.

Stationary points are $(-3,27)$ and $(1,-5)$ as required.

Nature:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} x & -4 & -3 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline f'(x) & +ve & 0 & -ve & 0 & +ve \end{array}$$

So $(-3,27)$ is a local maximum and $(1,-5)$ is a local minimum.
Solutions to $x^3-3x^2+4 = -x^2+x+2$ are the intersections of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, so the number of solutions is $3$.
$\dfrac{OM}{OA} = \tan 22^\circ$, so $h = 2000\tan 22^\circ = 808.5\ \text{m} = 808$ m to the nearest metre, as required.
$\dfrac{OM}{OB} = \tan 20^\circ$, so $OB = \dfrac{h}{\tan 20^\circ} = 2220.105\ \text{m} = 2220$ m to the nearest metre.

Bearing of $O$ from $B = 180^\circ + \angle B$ (in triangle $OAB$ with $OB = 2220$, $AB = 1000$, $OA = 2000$).

$\cos B = \dfrac{2220^2+1000^2-2000^2}{2\times 1000\times 2220} = 0.483$

$B = \cos^{-1}0.483 = 63.994^\circ$

Bearing of $O$ from $B = 180+64 = 244^\circ\text{T}$

$\dfrac{d^2V}{dt^2} = 2$, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$ does not have any stationary points. The maximum rate must therefore be at an endpoint ($t=0$ or $t=90$), as there are no points of inflexion.

When $t=0$, $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -180$ L/min; when $t=90$, $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 0$ L/min.

So the fastest draining rate is when $t=0$.

Total area $=$ area under $f(x)$ from $-1$ to $0$ $+$ area under $g(x)$ from $0$ to $1$.

$A = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^0 (x+1)\,dx + \int_0^1 (x-1)^2\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}+x\right]_{-1}^0 + \left[\dfrac{(x-1)^3}{3}\right]_0^1$

$= 0 - \left(\dfrac{(-1)^2}{2} + (-1)\right) + \left[0 - \dfrac{(-1)^3}{3}\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{3}$

$A = \dfrac{5}{6}\ \text{u}^2$
When $t=1$, $v = 2 - \dfrac{4}{1+1} = 2-2 = 0$. Velocity $=0$ when $t=1$, so the particle is at rest.

$d = \displaystyle\int v\,dt = \int\left(2-\dfrac{4}{t+1}\right)dt = 2t - 4\ln(t+1) + C$.

When $t=0$, $d=1$: $0 - 4\ln 1 + C = 1$, so $C=1$.

$d = 2t-4\ln(t+1)+1$.

At rest $t=1$: $d = 2(1) - 4\ln 2 + 1 = 3-4\ln 2 = 0.227$ m

The particle is only at rest when $t=1$, so the displacement curve has only one stationary point, at $t=1$. The acceleration at $t=1$ is $\dfrac{4}{(1+1)^2}$, which is positive, so the displacement curve has a local minimum at $t=1$ (concave up) and the displacement there is $0.227$, which is positive. Therefore displacement is always $\ge 0.227$, so always positive.

$r$ is a minimum when $r^2$ is a minimum.

$\dfrac{d(r^2)}{dt} = 20000t-12000 = 0$, so $2000(10t-6)=0$, $t = \dfrac{6}{10} = 0.6$ hours.

Check: $\dfrac{d^2(r^2)}{dt^2} = 2000(10) > 0$ for all $t$, so $r^2$ is concave up and the stationary point is a local minimum.

$r = \sqrt{r^2} = \sqrt{2000(5\times 0.6^2 - 6\times 0.6+5)} = \sqrt{6400}$

$r = 80$ km (minimum distance between cars).

Minimum height $= 1-0.4 = 0.6$ m.

Minimum occurs at $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of the period $= \dfrac{3}{4}\times 12 = 9$ hours, so the time is $8\text{ am}+9\text{ hours} = 5$ p.m.

We want $h\ge 1.2$: $1+0.4\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)\ge 1.2$, so $0.4\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)\ge 0.2$, $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)\ge\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\dfrac{\pi}{6}\le\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\le\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$, so $1\le t\le 5$.

The ship can enter the harbour between $8+1 = 9$ a.m. and $8+5=13$, i.e. 1 p.m.

notes: Solutions are handwritten, bundled in the same PDF (pages 36-56), and have no marking criteria, so marks_breakdown is null. Typos in paper: Q13 header '(1 marks)'; Q15 header '(4 marks' missing bracket; Q28 says 'Joseph K' then 'Josef K', and '11 students' though table lists 10 (plus the absent student); Q37(c) 'accelaration'. Q18(a): ambiguous wording 'willing to be vaccinated by either vaccine'; the printed solution takes this as P(both) = 1/5, while part (b)'s solution treats 38 of 50 as willing (so 'either' as 'at least one' would give 38/50 = 19/25). Needs checking/fixing in later step. Q32(a) printed solution gives F(x)=0 'otherwise' (should be 0 for x<1 and 1 for x>2). Q30(b) printed solution uses 0.8844 in the middle step but the table value is 0.8849 (result 0.5028 uses 0.8849). Q37(d) solution text kept as written. Page 7 (printed 7) is absent; page numbering skips from 6 to 8. Question figure for Q36 crop starts below the '(2 marks)' text so the top tip of the y-axis label is slightly cut. Q31(c) solution figure and Q33(a) solution figure are crops of handwritten scans (graph only). Q9 solution handwriting overlay not cropped (key A only). Q15 kept as one question since parts share the 'Differentiate' stem.
